g.text: Each line is one hash. Each dot is the median of up to 192 timings at that size.
The shaded band around a line shows how precisely its median is known (95% confidence); a deeper tint marks a less certain median.
A dot's shape marks the method the hash used at that size. The section "Code paths" at the bottom names each method.
Rate counts bytes or messages per second, time the nanoseconds per byte or message; the switch at right changes every plot.
The strip at the top narrows every plot to part of its inputs: drag an end of its band, or use the arrows at its ends.
Where a line splits in two, the timings ran at two different speeds; the note under the last plot says why.

svg.text: [*] Two speeds: at some sizes the timings fell into two clearly different speeds, so the line splits in two there, the rarer speed drawn fainter
in proportion to how rarely it occurred. A common cause is a chip with fast performance cores and slower efficiency cores, where the operating
system may run the work on either kind. Two programs sharing one part of the chip, or a virtual machine its host moves between cores, split speeds too.

g.data-summary: the method behind each dot shape, hash by hash
g.text: ▾ Code paths — the method behind each dot shape, hash by hash

svg.text: BLAKE3 · ● portable code, one chunk at a time, from the start (one input, pieces): Below four whole chunks (4 KiB), each chunk is hashed by the crate's portable code, one after
BLAKE3 · ◆ NEON vectors, four chunks at a time, from 4 KiB (one input, pieces): Four whole chunks fill the NEON vector units; from here most of the input runs four chunks at a
BLAKE3 · ● portable code, one chunk at a time, one message per call, from the start (batches): Each message is its own call; the size of the batch changes nothing.
SHA-256 · ● the CPU's SHA-256 instructions, from the start (one input, pieces): One method at every size.
SHA-256 · ● the CPU's SHA-256 instructions, one message per call, from the start (batches): Each message is its own call; the size of the batch changes nothing.
SHA-1DC · ● portable code with collision detection, from the start (one input, pieces): One method at every size.
SHA-1DC · ● portable code with collision detection, one message per call, from the start (batches): Each message is its own call; the size of the batch changes nothing.
BLAKE3 servil st · ● integer code, one call, from the start (one input, pieces): Inputs of one chunk (1 KiB) or less are hashed in one call of integer-only code that keeps its
BLAKE3 servil st · ◆ integer and NEON code side by side, from 1025 B (one input, pieces): Above one chunk the input is hashed several chunks at a time, up to fifteen per call:
some chunks on the integer units and the rest on the NEON vector units, at once. Below sixteen chunks this is the method; above, it hashes what SME2 leaves over.
BLAKE3 servil st · ■ SME2, sixteen chunks at a time, from 16 KiB (one input, pieces): Sixteen whole chunks fill the 512-bit vectors of the SME2 matrix unit; fewer than sixteen
left over go to the integer and NEON code. From 32 KiB each whole subtree of the input runs on SME2 alone, its parent nodes included.
BLAKE3 servil st · ▲ SME2 with integer code beside it, from 256 KiB (one input): From 256 KiB each whole subtree of up to 1 MiB runs on SME2 while the integer units hash two
chunks of every eighteen beside it.
BLAKE3 servil st · ● integer code, one message per call, from the start (batches): A single message runs the same one-call integer code as one input.
BLAKE3 servil st · ◆ integer and NEON code, up to nine messages at a time, from 128 B (batches): Two or more one-block messages are hashed together, up to eight on the NEON
vector units and one on the integer units at once; on SME2 this handles the messages left over below a group of sixteen.
BLAKE3 servil st · ■ SME2, sixteen messages at a time, from 1 KiB (batches): Sixteen one-block messages fill the SME2 matrix unit's vectors, one message per lane; fewer than
sixteen left over go to the integer and NEON code.
SHA-256 ring · ● the CPU's SHA-256 instructions, interleaved, from the start (one input, pieces): One method at every size.
SHA-256 ring · ● the CPU's SHA-256 instructions, interleaved, one message per call, from the start (batches): Each message is its own call; the size of the batch changes nothing.
BLAKE3 mt · ● on the calling thread, from the start: Up to one vector width of chunks, there is nothing to split.
BLAKE3 mt · ◆ split over Rayon's threads, from 8 KiB: Above that, the input splits in halves, again and again, and idle threads of the Rayon pool take them.
BLAKE3 servil mt · ● integer code, one call, from the start (one input, pieces): Inputs of one chunk (1 KiB) or less are hashed in one call of integer-only code that keeps its
BLAKE3 servil mt · ◆ integer and NEON code side by side, from 1025 B (one input, pieces): Above one chunk the input is hashed several chunks at a time, up to fifteen per call:
some chunks on the integer units and the rest on the NEON vector units, at once. Below sixteen chunks this is the method; above, it hashes what SME2 leaves over.
BLAKE3 servil mt · ■ SME2, sixteen chunks at a time, from 16 KiB (one input, pieces): Sixteen whole chunks fill the 512-bit vectors of the SME2 matrix unit; fewer than sixteen
left over go to the integer and NEON code. From 32 KiB each whole subtree of the input runs on SME2 alone, its parent nodes included.
BLAKE3 servil mt · ▲ split over threads, from 64 KiB (one input, pieces): From here the input is cut into whole subtrees that the calling thread and this crate's worker threads
(one per CPU beyond the first) hash at once: the calling thread on SME2 where it can, the others with integer and NEON code.
BLAKE3 servil mt · ● integer code, one message per call, from the start (batches): A single message runs the same one-call integer code as one input.
BLAKE3 servil mt · ◆ integer and NEON code, up to nine messages at a time, from 128 B (batches): Two or more one-block messages are hashed together, up to eight on the NEON
vector units and one on the integer units at once; on SME2 this handles the messages left over below a group of sixteen.
BLAKE3 servil mt · ■ SME2, sixteen messages at a time, from 1 KiB (batches): Sixteen one-block messages fill the SME2 matrix unit's vectors, one message per lane; fewer than
sixteen left over go to the integer and NEON code.
BLAKE3 servil mt · ▲ split over threads, from 64 KiB (batches): From here the batch is cut into ranges of messages that the calling thread and this crate's worker threads (one
per CPU beyond the first) hash at once, each with integer and NEON code.
ab-blake3 · ● portable code, from the start (one input): One method at every size: the crate's one-input function is written so it can also run while a program compiles, which
ab-blake3 · ● one message at a time, from the start (batches): Below sixteen messages, the batch function hashes each message on its own, one after another.
ab-blake3 · ◆ vectors, sixteen messages at a time, from 1 KiB (batches): From sixteen messages, each full group of sixteen goes through the blake3 crate's vector code (NEON
vectors, four chunks at a time); messages past the last full group are hashed one at a time.
